FDI has positive effects on economic growth in transition and developing economies.
FDI has a positive and significant impact on growth for developing countries, but not for transition economies.
FDI inflows are found to have a statistically significant positive effect on growth in developing countries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of FFD on growth in transition and developing countries.
investigating the economic and political determinants of the effects of foreign direct investment (FDI) on growth in a large number of developing and transition economies.
the effects of FFDI and human capital on growth in transition and developing countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a positive effect of FDI on economic growth in developing countries.
FDI inflows do have a significant positive effect on growth, particularly in developing countries, but not in transition countries.
FDI inflows have a positive and significant effect on growth in developing countries, but not in Transition economies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the results of this paper are consistent with the view that the effects of F DI on growth in developing countries are likely to depend upon a country’s level of political development, the level of its human capital endowment and the nature of its political regime.
FDI is a significant determinant of growth in transition and developing economies.
FDI is not a panacea for development in the transition and developing world.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FDI is not an unalloyed good for growth.
the effects of FFD on growth are not uniform across all regimes.
the growth effects of FDI are not universal and that these vary according to the regime type of host countries.
